ops.title: service: detect a disabled LaunchAgent as drift, now that verify() no longer silently re-enables
ops.description:
Landed in `881c1867` (the one-launchctl-classifier commit): `Controller.verify()` no longer issues `launchctl enable`. A read had been mutating, which is RC2 (replay-at-observe) and also fed a measured durable leak — `launchctl enable` writes a permanent root-owned override-DB entry per label that uninstall never removes (`service/controller.go:477,:581`).

**The gap this opens.** A label that is loaded-but-*disabled* — by the user, or by MDM — used to be silently re-enabled as a side effect of a no-op Converge. It no longer is, and nothing else notices: `verify` reports the agent as fine, so Converge reports no drift and takes no action. `install`/`reload` still enable on every load, so the condition only persists for an agent that is already installed and is not being reloaded.

**Why the fix is not just "put the enable back".** The healing model this remediation is converging on says reconcile *observes* and never replays; drift is typed and repaired by the converge step, not by a side effect of reading. So the correct shape is: `verify` observes disabled-ness and reports it as drift; the converge step enables. That also keeps the override-DB write on the deliberate path rather than the incidental one.

**What it needs.** Disabled state is not in `launchctl print` for the label — it lives in the override database, surfaced by `launchctl print-disabled gui/<uid>`, which lists labels with a `=> true|false`. That is a new observation verb in the classifier's world, so it should route through the `launchctlOutcome` boundary added in `881c1867` (`service/launchctl.go`) rather than parsing raw output at a call site.

Flagged rather than done by the classifier lane, deliberately and correctly — it was out of that lane's stated scope, and inventing an observation verb mid-lane is how scope creep produced the mess this remediation is unwinding.

ops.text: A disabled-but-loaded agent is reported as typed drift by Converge rather than silently ignored
verify() still issues no launchctl mutation — the enable happens on the converge path
The disabled observation routes through the launchctlOutcome classifier in service/launchctl.go, not raw output parsing at a call site
A test pins that a disabled agent produces drift, and that verify() alone changes nothing
